D6 REUSE COLLAPSE UNDER RESTRICTION (repair of the D5 limit): let d_g be the number of input variables gate g depends on. Under a truly random p-restriction, a reused gate stays a non-literal, non-constant reused gate only if >= 2 of its d_g variables stay live, so Pr <= C(d_g,2) p^2 <= p^2 d_g^2/2 (union over pairs) and E[gamma(C|rho)] <= sum_{g reused} min(1, p^2 d_g^2/2). With p = N^{beta+eps/5-1}: reused gates with d_g <= N^{1-beta-eta} contribute <= N^{-2 eta}, so only WIDE reused gates (d_g > N^{1-beta-eta}) can survive. Combined with AF: if P1, P2 hold, Gap-MCSP[N^beta] has no De Morgan circuit of size N^{1+eps} with at most N^{beta-2eta} wide reused gates (Markov over rho). Sanity check (dual-rail parity): the tree has ~N/2^j reused nodes with d_g = 2^j; sum_j (N/2^j) min(1,p^2 4^j) = Theta(pN) = Theta(k) survivors, matching counterexample 1 - those survivors are exactly the wide nodes (d_g >= 1/p). A*-REFUTER (owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). u_j = 1-P_j(n,j) if P_j answers within B, else 0 (j <= K); u_{K+1}=1; other bits 0; v = 0^n if b0=0, v = e_{K+1} if b0=1. Every P_j mismatches at position j, so A* outputs b0, while DISJ(u,v)=1-b0: R refutes A* at every large n without simulating A*'s stream. L_R={<n,i>: R(1^n)_i=1} is in DTIME(m^{O(sqrt log m)}); L_R is NOT in P (unconditional): a fixed m^c-time program for L_R would be enumerated and kept active, so A* would be correct on R(1^n) - this is a time-hierarchy diagonal, nothing beyond the hierarchy theorem. CC(R(1^n)) = O(m^2) (at most 2m+2 ones: DNF of minterms), so R is non-uniformly easy; the sparse algorithm A** (store the <= K+1 one-positions of x, O(m^2) space, check them against y) solves every R-instance unconditionally. SEED-FLOOR (proof of the D5 claim, seq 16768): if a distribution G on {0,1}^k has support size <= M (e.g. seed length l, M = 2^l), then some AND of t = floor(log2 M) + 1 <= k literals has |Pr_G - Pr_U| >= 2^{-t}: of the 2^t patterns on the first t coordinates at most M < 2^t are hit, a missed pattern has Pr_G = 0 and Pr_U = 2^{-t}. Hence fooling De Morgan formulas of size >= t with error delta forces log2 M >= log2(1/delta) - 1. In the D4/AF mechanism (error 2^{-r-2} for r surviving reused gates): seed >= r + 1, and since YES outputs G(z) o rho have circuit size <= N^beta, the support on the star coordinates is <= 2^{O(N^beta log N)}, so r <= O(N^beta log N). Consequence: every PRG instantiation of AF has polylog(1/delta)-exponent a >= 1 and covers at most N^{beta+o(1)} surviving reused gates; circuits with more surviving reuse must first be reduced by D6'/NORM.

JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; extends CHMY-SEED-FLOOR seq 17279 to the owner's proposal 'control the error of the whole state distribution jointly instead of per branching program'; CLAIMED). (1) What is needed is only ONE-SIDED: if M decides MCSP[s] correctly, it accepts every string of CC <= s and Pr_U[M=1] <= gamma := Pr_U[CC <= s] <= 2^{O(s log s) - N}; a contradiction follows as soon as Pr_G[M=1] < 1, i.e. G is a hitting set for the complement of M (density >= 1 - gamma). This is weaker than the two-sided 1/6 condition. (2) FLOOR for every analysis that uses only the decomposition M = OR_{alpha in A} P_alpha with each P_alpha a read-once BP of width <= w (any fixed order per alpha) and Pr_U[M=1] <= gamma: let H be the image of G (all CC <= s, so |H| <= 2^{O(s log s)} and |H| 2^{-N} <= gamma). A width-w ROBP in any fixed order accepts any prescribed set of <= w strings (one path per string, <= w distinct prefixes per level), so H is the union of ceil(|H|/w) such ROBPs; if ceil(|H|/w) <= |A| this OR is a member of the class, has acceptance measure |H| 2^{-N} <= gamma, and accepts all of H. Hence the analysis can succeed only if |H| > w |A|, i.e. s log s >= Omega(log w + log |A|). This holds for joint, one-sided, distribution-level error control (S0258/S0290-type compression of state distributions included) as long as the pieces are treated as generic ROBPs. (3) For CHMY Lemma 19, log(w |A|) = Theta(sqrt t log tq), so again mu >= 0.505 - o(1) at t = N^{1.01}. Lemma D'': along a curve in GL.det_n to f_0, the conormal of a multiplicity-one component of V(f_0) is an irreducible COMPONENT of the flat limit of conormals (all hypersurface conormals have dimension N-2); consequences: slotwise polar-degree domination and the bigraded Hilbert function bound H_{Con V}(a,b) <= H_{Con det_n}(a,b). Proposition Q: at the level of cycle classes this is equivalent to polar-degree domination (conormals of linear spaces give all unit classes). The kernel incidence of the cubic preprint is the conormal correspondence of det_n. Open obligation O1: an invariant of components of flat limits of GL-translates of Con(det_n), not determined by the class, bounded for all such limits and violated by Con(cone over V(per_m)) at n = omega(m^3).

structure.conclusion: CHMY-SEED-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; owner task 'improve the CHMY/Forbes-Kelley generator'; CLAIMED). Inputs: CHMY (ECCC TR20-103, local literature/sources/eccc-TR20-103) Lemma 19 (l.718: q-state time-t one-tape DTM = sum over alpha in A of ROBPs P_alpha of width exp(O(sqrt t log tq)), |A| <= (tq)^{O(sqrt t)}), Corollary 39 / Theorem 20 (generic ROBP PRG with error eps' = eps/|A|), Theorem 47 (needs MCSP[2^{mu n}] not in DTIME1[N^{1.01}] for a SMALL mu > 0), Corollary 17 (l.657, unconditional: MCSP[s] in DTIME1^O[N poly(s)] for some O in Sigma3^P, queries of length poly(s)), Lemma 21 (oracle queries of length l and fixed coins folded into q 2^l t states); SEED-FLOOR seq 17150 (support M => some AND of floor(log2 M)+1 literals has error >= 2^{-t}). (a) LEMMA: every distribution whose samples all have CC <= s and which eps'-fools all n-input ROBPs of width >= 2 satisfies s log s >= Omega(log(1/eps')). Proof: support <= #circuits of size s = 2^{O(s log s)}; an AND of literals is a width-2 ROBP; apply SEED-FLOOR. (b) In the CHMY architecture eps' = eps/|A| = eps (tq)^{-Theta(sqrt t)}, hence s >= Omega~(sqrt t log(tq)). For t = N^{1.01}, q = O(1): s >= N^{0.505-o(1)}, i.e. mu >= 0.505 - o(1), while Theorem 47 needs mu below the small constant of MMW. Forbes-Kelley (Theorem 38: seed O~(log(nw/eps')) log^3 n = O~(sqrt t log tq)) is already optimal in this architecture up to polylog factors. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): improving the generator recursion G_{i+1} = D_i xor (T_i and G_i), or any generic ROBP PRG, inside the Lemma-19 union-bound architecture, as a route to small mu. (c) Further unconditional constraint from Corollary 17 + Lemma 21 (deterministic Sigma3 oracle machine, no coins): no distribution on strings of CC <= s fools all (2^{poly(s)})-state DTMs of time N poly(s) (the folded Corollary-17 machine accepts all of them and rejects almost all uniform strings). Hence any improved generator for small mu must have a guarantee that FAILS at q = 2^{poly(s)} states, i.e. it must use that the attacked machine has few states. SURVIVING constructive directions (not lanes, recorded for the owner task): (i) a decomposition of time-N^{1.01} one-tape DTMs into <= 2^{N^{mu}} pieces (replacing Lemma 19's (tq)^{sqrt t} crossing-sequence guesses), or (ii) an analysis that fools the specific machine without the union bound over A (cancellations among P_alpha), in both cases exploiting q = O(1).

CONV-D (owner weakening 2026-11-26, director check; the obligation of TRUNC2 seq 17202 in exponent form). F_beta = Gap-MCSP[N^beta/(c log N), N^beta]; under NP subset SIZE[n^a], QO1 gives circuits S(F_beta) <= O(N^{1+K beta}), K = K(a). CJW20-GAP (seq 17198; any polylog gap factor, the proof's knobs are independent) gives L(F_beta) >= N^{2+beta-xi} for every xi > 0. A problem-dependent conversion L(F_beta) <= O(S(F_beta)^{2-d(beta)}) contradicts it iff d(beta)(1+K beta) > (2K-1)beta + xi; choosing xi = beta this holds whenever d(beta) > 2K beta/(1+K beta). ST2 INDEPENDENT TRANSFER, STRENGTHENED (author Claude family; owner's sec. 9 argument with P = NP replaced by NP subset P/poly): let S be polylog-uniform AC0_d[2^{m^k}] with r CX rounds, uniformity time m^u. Bit i of X_j is a Sigma_{d'}-TIME[poly(m, L_j, log b)] predicate g_j(i, b, D_<j) with random access to the earlier answers D_<j (padding zeros beyond the description). Assume NP subset P/poly, so PH subset P/poly and Sigma_{d'} has circuits of size n^{c}. Induction: if every earlier answer has size <= m^{K_i}, hardwiring b and D_<j gives a circuit for X_j of size m^{K_j}, K_j = c*O(K_{j-1} + k + u), independent of b. For b > K* = max_j K_j the answer 'a circuit of size m^{K_j} for X_j' is admissible in every round (Teacher only has to exist, no uniformity needed), so X_r has circuit complexity <= m^{K*} < m^b at every large N: S fails for all b > K*. Hence: absolute protocol => NP notsubset P/poly (stronger than Thm 1.7's P != NP). Uses neither Lemma 5.4 nor SearchMCSP.

BIAS-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; check of the owner's global Fourier error balance for the Forbes-Kelley step; CLAIMED). Owner's identities verified: (i) Parseval + Cauchy-Schwarz: sum_S |f^(S)| <= sqrt(A) for f in {0,1} with A accepted inputs; (ii) for independent D_i, T_i, G_i: b_{D xor (T and G)}(S) = b_D(S) E_T b_G(S cap T), so |b_{G_{i+1}}(S)| <= delta_i and Delta <= delta_i sqrt(A); (iii) signed S0290 convolution f^(S) = 2^{-N} sum_{u_1+..+u_q >= T} prod_j D_{j,S}(u_j) for disjoint components (Walsh characters are multiplicative over the components). LEMMA (unconditional): for every F subset {0,1}^N with |F| = A and every distribution Y supported in F, max_{S nonempty} |b_Y(S)| >= (1 - A 2^{-N}) / sqrt(A). Proof: apply (i) to f = 1_F: 1 - A 2^{-N} = E f(Y) - E f(U) = sum_{S nonempty} f^(S) b_Y(S) <= max|b_Y| sqrt(A). CONSEQUENCE: with F = {CC <= s}, A <= 2^{O(s log s)}, the bias delta < 1/(6 sqrt A) required by the owner's balance cannot be achieved by ANY distribution whose outputs all have CC <= s; a generator that meets it necessarily has outputs of CC > s. The gap 'CC(G(z)) <= N^{mu+o(1)} versus the needed <= N^mu' is therefore not a lower-order technicality but a counting impossibility. Reason: the estimate uses only A and not the resources of M, so it would apply equally to f = 1_F itself. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): fooling the MCSP algorithm through a bias/Fourier-L1 bound that depends only on the number of accepted inputs, for every mu. Any working generator analysis must use the time/state bound of M (consistent with seq 17279 (c) and seq 17284).

CJ2 SUFFIX WITHOUT SELECTION (owner derivation, checked): for u != v with sigma_A(u) = sigma_A(v) let y = u AND NOT v if that is nonzero (then DISJ(u,y)=0, DISJ(v,y)=1), else y = v AND NOT u (roles swapped); the case test is an OR of n bits (AC0). A answers both instances equally, so one of F1(n)=(u_n,y_n), F2(n)=(v_n,y_n) is wrong at each such n, and by pigeonhole one fixed family is wrong infinitely often; the theorem only needs existence of R_A. CC(y) <= CC(u)+CC(v)+O(1), so y stays simple. Remaining W-D obligation: uniform (polylogtime-uniform AC0) colliding prefix families u_n != v_n for every admissible deterministic A, infinitely often.

Tangent-space bound (Fall D tool): for any singular point X of perm_n, rank Hess(perm_n)(X) <= n^2 - dim_X Sigma, where Sigma=Sing(V(perm_n))={grad perm_n=0}. In particular the torus orbit (dim <= 2n-1) gives rank <= n^2-(2n-1), recovering the connected torus bound.
structure.justification: Hess(perm_n) is the Jacobian of the map grad(perm_n): C^{n^2}->C^{n^2}; Sigma = {grad perm_n = 0} is its zero locus, so the Zariski tangent space T_X Sigma = ker Hess, giving dim ker Hess >= dim_X Sigma, i.e. rank Hess <= n^2 - dim_X Sigma. Consequence: M_5=14 would follow if every connected singular point lies in a component of Sigma(perm_5) of dimension >= 11. Whether dim Sigma(perm_5) >= 11 on connected components is OPEN (singular-locus geometry of perm, 2024 literature).

structure.conclusion: D3 BASIS: B2 -> De Morgan for circuits: each XOR/XNOR gate becomes 3 De Morgan gates and both of its children acquire fan-out 2. A B2 circuit of size S with r reused gates and t parity gates becomes a De Morgan circuit of size <= 3S with <= r+2t reused gates. For FORMULAS the conversion is not polynomially size-preserving in the needed exponent (B2 shrinkage exponent is 1, parity), so CJW20-type bounds hold in the De Morgan basis; B2 results follow only through r+2t. CHOPRS20 almost-formulas are De Morgan, so frontier C is basis-consistent.

structure.conclusion: FACTOR-WITNESS (director, 2026-11-26, answering the owner's T07-S0290 synthesis question; CLAIMED). Split the table into k aligned blocks x_1..x_k. Product factorisation (AND over blocks of [x_i has an a'-circuit]) or score folding (sum_i min_{C_i} D_i(C_i)) replaces the SHARED witness (exists C forall i) by independent witnesses (forall i exists C_i). Facts: CC(x_i) <= CC(x)+O(m) and CC(x) <= sum_i CC(x_i) + O(km). (i) VALID for Gap-MCSP[a,b], b = 10ma, when k <= c1 m: YES gives every block <= a+O(m) =: a'; NO gives some block > (b-O(km))/k > a'. (ii) INVALID for k >= c2 m: let block i be the table of an independent random circuit of size a/2; every block test accepts (CC <= a/2 < a', every D*_i = 0), while there are 2^{k Omega(a log a)} such tables and circuits of size S number 2^{O(S log S)}, so some such x has CC(x) >= Omega(k a) > b. The window is Theta(log N) components, tight up to constants. (iii) In the valid window the factorised formula is a sum of k Gap-MCSP formulas on N/k bits with constant gap, covered by CJW20-GAP (the proof's knobs are independent of the gap factor): exponent unchanged (BLOCK-EMB seq 17180, ratio invariance). MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): component factorisation / score folding with independent per-component witnesses as an exponent-gaining conversion, for any number of components. Consequence for T07 (seq 16758, A1 semantic T07 seq 16774) + S0290: the enumeration over cut assignments can be factorised only where the coupling through the shared witness is removed, which is (i)-(ii); a remaining route needs a compression of the shared-witness coupling that is not a product over components. Not located in the current registry: the CAPP steps S0258/S0290 (other question state); their full proofs were not re-read here.

structure.conclusion: ST3 SANDWICH - EXACT STRENGTH OF THE TARGET (author Claude family): converse with r = 0: if some fixed L in PH (Sigma_d, time m^u) has a.e. superpolynomial circuit complexity (for every b, CC(L_m) > m^b for all large m), then S(1^N, b) = tt(L_m) is a 0-round absolute protocol (depth d+O(1), size 2^{poly(m)}, uniformity poly(m), b ignored). So: [exists L in PH, a.e. superpolynomial] => [absolute 0-round protocol] => [absolute r-round protocol] => NP notsubset P/poly => P != NP. The Teacher rounds move the target at most between the a.e. and the i.o. form of 'PH notsubset P/poly'. RIGOROUS EXCLUSION: 'counterexamples as the source of hardness' gives no leverage beyond a PH circuit lower bound; every round transformation is, under PH subset P/poly, a bounded-complexity composition, so fail-fast control B is exhaustive, not heuristic. The owner's controls A and B are instances of ST2.

SEP-MERGE-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director checked; CLAIMED). Gap-MCSP[a,b], b = N^beta, a = b/(10m). Split the table into q equal dyadic blocks. Any realisation F = OR_{sigma in {0,1}^w} AND_{j<=q} F_{j,sigma}(x_j) (arbitrary local F_{j,sigma}) needs w >= B/2 = Omega_beta(N^beta) for q = C_beta m. Proof checked: B = Theta(a log a) a power of 2 with every B-bit table of circuit size <= a (Lupanov); the periodic tables y^{N/B} are 2^B YES instances (the circuit reads only the low log B index bits); blocks are dyadic of size >= B, so each block contains whole periods and distinct y give distinct block restrictions; a sigma accepting k patterns accepts their k^q block-wise mixtures (product of the A_{j,sigma}), none of which may be a NO instance, and at most 2^{O(b log b)} tables have CC <= b, so k <= 2^{O(b log b / q)} <= 2^{B/2} for q = C_beta m; hence 2^w >= 2^{B/2}. Tight up to a log factor: sigma = a size-b circuit description (O(b log b) bits) with F_{j,sigma}(x_j) = [x_j = block j of tt(sigma)] is a valid realisation, so w = Theta~_beta(N^beta). Type: nondeterministic q-party number-in-hand cover / fooling-set bound; novelty not checked. SCOPE: (1) block-faithful: after fixing sigma no condition reads two blocks; the recursive elimination of SEP-ELIM-LB flattens by distributivity to this form with w <= (#leaves) W_path, so with leaves = blocks W_path >= Omega_beta(N^beta / log N). (2) NOT a formula lower bound: formula size corresponds to Karchmer-Wigderson games (seq 3616), not to rectangle covers; the owner's equality example (cover 2^B, formula O(qB)) shows the gap. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): block-faithful separator / conditional-state enumeration, including a conditional S0290-style score convolution over shared variables in the OR_sigma AND_j form, as an exponent-gaining conversion for Gap-MCSP.

Any 'solution-count mod 3' Gal matrix A[u,v] = #solutions of the clause system u union v, taken mod 3, is identically zero: Boolean count = 0 because v is UNSAT; GF(3) count is 0 (inconsistent) or 3^d with d >= 1 (the all-ones direction j is always in the kernel), hence 0 mod 3. Solution counts mod 3 carry no information for positive 1-in-3; any useful count needs the j-direction quotiented out (count lines, i.e. 3^(d-1)).

ACCEPTANCE-TRIE (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting of seq 17306/17314: for an accepting crossing signature alpha (crossing records include state, time and input-head position), R_alpha = prod_j R_{alpha,j}, a_{alpha,j} = |R_{alpha,j}|, sum_alpha prod_j a_{alpha,j} = A (accepted inputs, disjoint by determinism). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (i) the trie of R_{alpha,j} has <= a_{alpha,j}+1 nodes per level (reject sink included), so w_{alpha,j} <= min(2^{O(B+log t)}, a_{alpha,j}+1); (ii) the per-alpha ROBP reads the parts J_{alpha,1}, J_{alpha,2}, ... one after another (legitimate: Forbes-Kelley fools arbitrary-order ROBPs) and collapses to accept/reject at part boundaries, so its width is max_j w_{alpha,j}; (iii) splitting each R_{alpha,j} into ceil(a/2^h) pieces of size <= 2^h gives an exact disjoint OR of K'(h) = sum_alpha prod_j ceil(a_{alpha,j}/2^h) ROBPs of width <= 2^h+1, and K'(h) = sum_alpha |R_alpha| 2^{-Phi_h(alpha)} = A E_X[2^{-Phi_h}] (X uniform on accepted inputs), log(w'K') <= h + 1 + log A - P(h). NEW LOWER BOUND (director): ceil(a/2^h) >= 1, so K'(h) >= K_acc := number of accepting signatures with R_alpha nonempty >= 2^{H(alpha(X))} for EVERY distribution X on accepted inputs; hence log(w'K') >= max(h, log K_acc). Replacing prefixes by residual (Myhill-Nerode) classes lowers the width further but leaves K' >= K_acc unchanged. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the trie attacks only point 1 of seq 17306 (width), never point 2 (crossing count); with the floor of seq 17284(2) any success needs s log s >~ log K_acc. (2) With seq 17314 on the Lupanov family: K_acc >= 2^{(rb-L)/(r-1)}, so for multiplicity r > L/b the trie gives no gain over the floor regime. (3) Jensen: P(h) <= E Phi_h <= E sum_j min(h, log a_{alpha,j}) <= E log|R_alpha| = log A - H(alpha(X)). So log(w'K') = N^{o(1)} REQUIRES (a) H(alpha(X)) <= N^{o(1)} and (b) E sum_j min(h, log a_{alpha,j}) >= log A - N^{o(1)} with h = N^{o(1)}: a typical accepted input has >= N^{mu-o(1)} information-carrying parts, each with <= 2^{N^{o(1)}} local completions, while its whole crossing signature has N^{o(1)} bits of entropy, i.e. the accepted set is up to 2^{N^{o(1)}} pieces a union of products with tiny factors and M is almost oblivious on accepted inputs across N^{mu} block visits. (4) The trade-off moves from the block length B to the local acceptance sizes: one block gives K_acc = 1, a = A, log w' = log A, which is exactly seq 17284(2). (5) The folded Cor-17 machine (seq 17279 (c)) is a correct decider, so (a)+(b) fails for it; a proof of (a)+(b) must use q = O(1). structure.conclusion: A*-STRENGTH (director, 2026-11-26; CLAIMED). (i) The open step 'L_R in PH' implies P != NP at once (L_R in PH minus P gives PH != P); A* is only the device certifying L_R not in P. More generally any refuter R* of A* (infinitely often) whose bit function is in PH gives a PH language outside P: the route is at least as strong as P != NP, not a reduction of it. (ii) L_R is hard for DTIME(m^{sqrt(log m)/2}) under polynomial-time reductions: for M deciding L' in that time, encode w in the m-bit number n_w and take the fixed program Q='decode w from n, run M(w)' of constant rank j0; then w in L' iff <n_w,j0> not in L_R. Hence L_R in PH iff (up to the constant in the exponent) DTIME(m^{Theta(sqrt log m)}) is contained in PH - a superpolynomial-time inclusion strictly stronger than P != NP. Relative to a PSPACE-complete oracle A, PH^A = P^A while the relativized time hierarchy keeps DTIME^A(m^{sqrt log m}) outside P^A, so the open step is false relative to A: any proof must be non-relativizing. (iii) Corrections to the 2026-11-26 review note: 'P=NP gives only polynomial, not polylogarithmic time' is wrong, since poly(m) = polylog(n); the refuter need not simulate A* over the stream (A*-REFUTER).

Contrapositive with CJW20-T5.5-GAP: every cut K of every correct De Morgan circuit of size S has |B_K^+| >= N^{2+beta-eps}/(2S+1).

EXCLUSION E-LEVIN (mechanism, not the statement): (a) for Levin's universal search U and every fixed algorithm A that outputs SAT witnesses, t_U(F) <= 2^{|A|} (t_A(F) + v(|F|)) with v the witness check time; hence 'U runs in polynomial time on all satisfiable F' <=> P = NP, and a lower bound for U is up to a constant factor a lower bound for every algorithm - the quantifier over algorithms is not removed. (b) Relative to an oracle A with P^A = NP^A (BGS, seq 3), U^A runs in polynomial time; every argument that uses U only through simulation and diagonalization relativizes and cannot show U superpolynomial. Excluded: pure simulation/diagonalization against U. Not excluded: arguments that use the Cook-Levin encoding of U's run non-black-box (short encodings of long computations); the only mechanism known to work there is the algorithmic method of Williams (succinct SAT), whose proven reach is NEXP/NQP lower bounds against ACC-type classes, not P != NP.

ADAPT-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED; strengthens NONADAPT-LB seq 17222). b = N^beta, a = b/(10m), beta fixed. (i) Small YES circuits: split the m index bits into q = O(1/beta) groups of beta m/2 bits, decode every group completely (O_beta(N^{beta/2}) = o(a) gates); each one-position is then an AND of q decoded lines, so ANY set of r = a/(2q) = Theta_beta(b/m) ones has an a-circuit (previously r = Theta(a/m)). (ii) A uniform table with exactly R = C_beta b ones is a NO instance with prob 1-o(1): C(N,R) = 2^{Omega(R log(N/R))} against 2^{O(b log(b+m))} circuits. (iii) A one-sided algorithm (YES always accepted) cannot reject while it has seen <= r ones, since the table with exactly the observed ones is a YES instance consistent with every answer. Each new adaptive query hits a one with prob <= R/(N-t), so E X_t <= tR/(N-t) and Pr[reject] <= Pr[X_t > r] <= O_beta(t m/N); averaging over the NO-heavy distribution gives a fixed NO instance, so t = Omega_beta(N/log N) for adaptive and non-adaptive one-sided algorithms. Director scope note: CJW20 and CONV-D allow TWO-SIDED error; for two-sided algorithms the same distributions (YES: uniform r-subset, NO: uniform R-subset) give only t = Omega(N/R) = Omega_beta(N^{1-beta}) (views are all-zero with prob >= 1 - tR/N under both). Query bounds of order N/polylog do not constrain CONV-D, whose formulas have size >= N anyway; they exclude only bit-selection (sampling) as the conversion mechanism.

TRUNC (owner construction, director check; CLAIMED). D^(tau)_I=min(tau,D_I) composes exactly: D^(tau)_{I u J}=min(tau, D^(tau)_I + D^(tau)_J). Node state: BOT if no a-circuit is tau-close on I, else (C_I, E_I) with |E_I|<tau, S=O(a log a + tau m)=O(N^beta) bits; BOT at any node implies D* >= tau (reject). Director: (C_I,E_I) is LOSSLESS for x_I and is itself a circuit of size <= a + c m tau <= b (correction by minterms), so the scheme is exactly an MMW tree whose gates are GAP-Merge gates (find any tau-close a-circuit, must succeed when an exact one exists); FOURIER-SUP does not apply because far tables all map to BOT. DILEMMA (director): tau=1 gives exact gates, so MERGE-EXACT-LB applies and local conversion fails; tau>1 gives gates outside CJW20 but the root then decides only Gap-MCSP, and CJW20 Thm 5.5 (exact, fixed threshold) gives no contradiction. A contradiction then needs a Gap-MCSP formula lower bound N^{2-delta+K beta}; the book's best Gap bound is far below that (MECH-RANGE seq 17158), so this horn is the QO2/Q2 obligation (eps/beta -> infinity). CORRECTION of the review note's item 6: comparing N^{2-delta+K beta} with N^{2+beta-xi} is valid only for EXACT MCSP. Open check: whether CHOPRS Lemma 22 (ECC transfer exact -> approximate MCSP) keeps both the YES side (CC(Enc x) <= poly CC(x)) and formula cost; the paper is not in the local literature.

MMW-UNFOLD (cost of the K1/MMW route, Q-5d167697b4; MMW19 Lemma 3.1 as verified in seq 10407: size O~(N s/l), depth O(log N / log l), Circuit-Min-Merge[s] gates with l-bit input, l >= s^2; tree with fan-out 1, seq 9992): replacing every gate by a De Morgan formula of size l^b and unfolding, each input bit of a gate is read up to l^{b-1} times on average, so the child subformula is copied that often per level; over depth log N/log l the total formula size is about N^{b+O(beta)}. A contradiction with CJW20 (N^{2+beta-xi}) therefore needs b < 2 - Theta(beta): the GATE function Circuit-Min-Merge[s] on l = N^{2beta} bits must have SUBQUADRATIC formulas. NP subset P/poly gives the gates circuits of size l^a and no formula bound at all (even NP subset Formula[poly] gives only some fixed b, not b < 2). Hence the middle formula L(C_MMW) <= N^{2-delta} s^K is the R-MCSP-type obligation for an MCSP-like function at scale l (self-similar), not a weaker obligation. Open as before; it does not bypass R-MCSP.

K0 (unconditional depth class for COV1): a De Morgan circuit of depth D unfolds to a formula with <= 2^D leaves; a B2 gate is a De Morgan formula using each input at most twice, so B2 depth D gives <= 4^D leaves. With CJW20-T5.5-GAP: Gap-MCSP[N^beta/(Km), N^beta] has no De Morgan circuit of depth < (2+beta-eps)log2 N and no B2 circuit of depth < (1+beta/2-eps/2)log2 N, of any size. This is the full reach of the verified results under the MMW19 joint size-depth condition: Thm 1.4 b.3 needs depth poly(s) >= polylog N; b.2 (NC1 conclusion only) needs every c log N.

D4 REUSE-TO-CORRELATION DECOMPOSITION (exact): let C be a De Morgan circuit with gamma gates g_1..g_gamma of fan-out > 1 and S gates. For a in {0,1}^gamma let F_a(x) = AND_j [P_j(x,a) = a_j] AND P_out(x,a), where P_j, P_out are the principal formulas (CHOPRS20 Thm 30) with reused gates replaced by constants a. Then L(F_a) <= S+gamma, the F_a have pairwise disjoint supports and C = OR_a F_a. For any two distributions Y, Z: Pr_Y[C]-Pr_Z[C] = sum_a (Pr_Y[F_a]-Pr_Z[F_a]), so some formula F_a of size <= S+gamma has advantage >= Adv(C)/2^gamma. Reuse costs a factor 2^gamma in CORRELATION, not in size (T07 pays it in size).

MECH-RANGE (parameter check against OPS21/Q2, seq 16795-16796): in AF with a PRG of seed s^{c+o(1)} (CKLM19: c = 1/3, seq 16757), stars >= N^{beta+eta/2} force p >= N^{beta+eta/2-1}; with the unconditional worst case s = p L, L = N^{1+eps} (D4-SIM), seed <= N^{beta-eta} needs c(beta + eta/2 + eps) <= beta - eta, so eps/beta < 1/c - 1 (c = 1/3: eps < 2beta). Hence eps(beta)/beta stays bounded for every fixed c and the mechanism cannot reach Q2 without a structural change. Two levers only: (i) c -> 0, a PRG for size-s De Morgan formulas with seed s^{o(1)}, which implies a function in E without polynomial-size De Morgan formulas (open, far beyond the known n^{3-o(1)}); (ii) a bound on the number m of principal formulas: with a Tal-type forest bound (P2) s <~ p^2 L + p sqrt(m L), Q2 requires m <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta} at total size N^{1+eps} with eps/beta -> infinity. The 'fundamental change' asked for by the owner is therefore a reduction of m (count of reused gates), not of W; this is a necessary condition, not a construction.

Let J_1..J_l be a FIXED (input-independent) family with |J_i| <= N^{1-zeta}. Uniform table with exactly R = D b ones (NO w.p. 1-o(1), as in ADAPT-LB seq 17227). By ADAPT-LB (i) any r = Theta_beta(b/m) ones have an a-circuit, so J_i is an anti-checker only if X_i = |J_i n ones| >= r. Hypergeometric tail: Pr[X_i >= r] <= (e|J_i|R/(N r))^r = (O_beta(m N^{-zeta}))^r = 2^{-Omega_{beta,zeta}(b)}. Union bound: for l <= 2^{c b} (c small) some NO instance has no anti-checker in the family. So a fixed family needs l >= 2^{Omega_{beta,zeta}(N^beta)} members. Any rule using only the family's consistency bits sees on that NO instance exactly what it sees on 0^N (a YES instance), so it accepts; an AND-of-tests formula over such a family has >= l leaves. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): fixed families of sublinear anti-checker candidates, any polynomial (even 2^{c N^beta}) size. NOT excluded: input-dependent anti-checkers; sets of size N^{1-o(1)}. CORRECTION of the scope note in seq 17222 ('does NOT constrain families'): fixed families are constrained by this count.

Slice route: level-m slices of f_n are coNP-hard (padding); monotone and general circuit size are polynomially related on slices (Berkowitz), so a superpolynomial monotone bound for them would prove P != NP (equivalent reformulation). Span-program analogue: mSP and SP polynomially related on slices, loss SP >= (mSP - 2N)/(N-1): all PNP-001 bounds (<= N+1) vanish under transfer. Generic Gal constructions on slices are natural-proofs-blocked (assuming NC^1 PRFs); a method must use function-specific structure.

(C1) Positive 1-in-3: S SAT iff the GF(3) solution set of {sum_{i in C} x_i = 1} contains a vector with <= 2 distinct values (j = all-ones is in the kernel; y - a j is Boolean). (C2) f_n = INCONS_n OR M_n with INCONS ideal of size N, so mSP_GF3(M_n) >= mSP_GF3(f_n) - N. (C3) Minimal GAP cores (Boolean-UNSAT, GF(3)-consistent, minimal) have GF(3)-independent rows, hence <= n-1 clauses, solution dimension n-|S|. Exact: n=6 900 cores (all size 5, 3 orbits), n=7 62,370 (8,190 size 5; 54,180 size 6). See theory/T44.

Generalization of the two-value criterion to positive 1-in-k over GF(p): (i) the all-ones vector j is in the kernel iff p | k (solutions form lines x + lambda j); (ii) a 0/1 vector with clause sums = 1 (mod p) has clause sums exactly 1 iff k <= p (sums lie in 0..k, next admissible value is 1+p). Hence 'S SAT iff Sol_p(S) contains a vector with <= 2 values' holds exactly for k = p: (3,3) and (5,5) yes; (4,2) no - GF(2) sees 'odd number true', not 'exactly one'; (3,2) no - j not in the kernel. GF(p)-blind MUS in the D-018 sense are defined only for k = p.
